knowledge_gaps: Fixing the final item controls immediate recency, but permuting earlier items changes both their order and distance from the target. Ranking damage therefore supports dependence on the original arrangement; it does not isolate sequence structure from positional recency or distribution shift.

Reproducibility needs explicit handling of tied scores, duplicate-item permutations and unchanged histories, bootstrap settings, and stable per-user random seeds. Five permutations may leave substantial randomization uncertainty; a user bootstrap alone does not separately quantify that uncertainty.

Training-prefix measurements cannot distinguish learned temporal structure from memorized transitions. The report acknowledges this limitation, but should narrow its claimed usefulness accordingly. Originality 4 is reasonable; implementation difficulty 2 may understate the statistical and reproducibility work.
